summary: Backend-only testing of ProximityMap AI (indoor navigation + proximity marketing) API. 16/16 pytest tests passed covering health, floorplans, beacons, aisles, products, positioning, proximity and routing. Verified no MongoDB _id leak in any response, cascade delete, single-active-floorplan invariant, weighted RSSI centroid biases toward strong beacon, and routing waypoints start near origin and end at product.

minor.issue: ScanReading.source default is 'ble' so caller can omit it; OK but undocumented. No upper bound on readings list (potential DoS with very large body) - not blocking.

Beacons that go stale are reported online=False at read time but the persisted document still has online=True from heartbeat. Inconsistency if other consumers read raw doc; consider clearing online via TTL job.

build_grid() ignores `aisles` param and never blocks any cells, so A* always returns a straight diagonal path regardless of aisles. Aisles are effectively decorative; turn-by-turn directions will not route AROUND shelves. This is a functional gap vs. the user-described 'routing arrow + turn-by-turn directions' feature, but it does not break API contract.
Returns null body (not 404) when no active plan exists; response_model Optional[FloorPlan] accepts null. Acceptable but client must null-check.
All DELETE endpoints return 200 with {ok:true} even when the id does not exist. Idempotent but does not signal not-found.

action_items: Optional: make build_grid() actually mark aisle interiors as blocked (or treat aisles as shelves and pathways as inverse) so routing produces realistic turn-by-turn paths around shelves, not straight diagonals.
Optional: return 404 on DELETE of unknown ids for clearer client feedback.
Optional: add server-side TTL/background task to flip beacon.online=false after >30s without heartbeat (currently only computed at read time).
critical_code_review_comments: build_grid() takes `aisles` arg but never uses it - dead code path; routing is essentially Manhattan-diagonal A* on empty grid.
datetime.fromisoformat in beacon listing relies on now_iso() format including +00:00; works on Py3.11 but could fail on older Pythons - acceptable here.
rssi==0 short-circuit in rssi_to_distance is unusual (real RSSI is negative); fine as a sentinel.
CORS allow_origins='*' with allow_credentials=True is technically invalid per CORS spec (browsers ignore credentials with wildcard); acceptable for local Windows deployment but flag for production.

Single server.py is ~580 lines - still under the 700 LOC threshold but approaching limit; consider splitting routers (floorplans/beacons/products/positioning/routing) into modules for maintainability.
No pagination on list endpoints (to_list(500/2000)); fine for current scale.
seed_data_creation: Test fixtures create TEST_-prefixed floorplans, 4 corner beacons with BLE MACs AA:AA:AA:AA:AA:01-04, and transient aisles/products. All fixtures clean up via DELETE.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is fully working. Pytest file at /app/backend/tests/test_proximitymap.py covers all endpoints. Known functional gap: routing A* grid has no real obstacles (aisles arg unused in build_grid), so paths are direct diagonals - main agent must decide whether shelves should block routing. No _id leakage observed in any response.
rca of the issue: N/A - no bugs to root-cause; only design-level observations above.
